title: Micro Fiction
sub: Tiny original stories, a paragraph or two each.

cards.title: The Last Light on the Street
text: Every other porch light on the block had gone out by eleven, but hers stayed on, the way it had every night since he left for the base.
She told the neighbors it was for the mail carrier, or for burglars, or for nobody in particular. She never told them it was so the street would look, from a distance, exactly like it used to.
cards.takeaway: Small rituals can carry a hope too big to say out loud.

cards.title: Two Minutes Before the Bell
text: The substitute teacher found the note folded into a paper airplane on his desk: "We know you’re nervous. We were too, our first day. — Room 14."
He read it twice, put it in his pocket, and picked up the marker with a steadier hand than he’d had all morning.
cards.takeaway: Kindness from an unexpected direction changes how a moment feels.

cards.title: The Apartment With No Nameplate
text: For six years the mailbox for 4C stayed blank while every other slot in the building had a name, a sticker, a joke.
When the new tenant finally wrote her name on a strip of tape, three neighbors knocked that same week, just to say welcome.
cards.takeaway: A small, ordinary signal can be the only invitation people are waiting for.
